name: spring_piston_helium_dynamic
title: Spring-loaded piston with helium: damped dynamic oscillation
summary: A steel piston latched in a well-insulated cylinder encloses helium at 400 kPa and 290 K; a compressed spring in the evacuated compartment pushes it back. When the latch is released the piston oscillates, damped by dynamic friction, while the gas expands and cools following the ideal-gas law. Newton's law is integrated in time (INTEGRAL) and the model returns the trajectory of the piston position, pressure, volume and temperature over 1 s.

verification.summary: Against the solution stored in the original EES file (hand-converted from kPa/K/kJ/kmole): re-run at the stop time of the stored EES run (t = 0.7212 s) gives 23 common variables, 6 differ (rtol=0.001), of which 4 physics diffs (vel 3.02e-01, acc 6.26e-03, T 3.91e-03) are the EES integration phase error, confirmed by an independent RK4 integration that agrees with CoolSolve to 2e-6 m on x; statics agree to 1.01e-04. The 722-row trajectory agrees with the integral table stored in the file to 4e-3 on x.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models/EES_library/spring.EES (29 variable records) and the integral table stored in the same file (722 filled rows, t = 0 to 0.721 s); independent Runge-Kutta 4 integration of the equations of the model
verification.notes: compare_solution.py --ees-units of the model re-run at the stop time of the stored EES run (time_final = 0.7212471652 s): 23 common variables, 6 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 1 (SF, an animation scale factor not imported); only in CoolSolve: 4 (T_abs, T_1_abs and the built-in constants pi, R#). The six differing variables: k_fric (the reference stores 0.01 kN-s/m, which --ees-units does not convert; 0.01 kN-s/m = 10 N-s/m, the value of the model), time_final (the value of the re-run itself) and the four physics diffs acc 6.26e-03, F_net 6.26e-03, T 3.91e-03, vel 3.02e-01. x (1.90e-04), P (4.91e-04), V (1.90e-04) and time (0) agree. The velocity deviation is a phase effect at the end of a lightly damped oscillation of period 0.055 s: an independent RK4 integration (step 1e-5 s) of the same equations gives x = 0.6805755 m against CoolSolve 0.680577 m at t = 0.7212 s, and confirms the EES stored trajectory as the outlier (its phase lags by about 0.5 ms). Against the 722 filled rows of the EES integral table (hand-converted kPa/K): max relative deviation 4.952e-03 on x (3.98e-03 m absolute), 7.858e-03 on P (1208 Pa), 4.951e-03 on V, 2.457e-01 on T at t = 0.11 s where T crosses the 0.01 °C of the reference (0.79 K absolute over the whole table); the statics agree to 1.01e-04 on c_v (EES vs CoolProp helium). At t = 1 s the model gives x = 0.695414 m, vel = 0.106138 m/s, P = 136538 Pa, T = -43.6873 °C against RK4 x = 0.695414 m, vel = 0.105356 m/s, T = -43.6861 °C.
